directAnswer: You can check an IP address using the command line or through online tools. For local IP addresses, use 'ipconfig' on Windows or 'ifconfig' on macOS/Linux.
summary: This guide provides methods to check both local and public IP addresses across different platforms.

sections.heading: Checking Local IP Address
sections.body: To find your local IP address, you can use the command line interface on your device.

sections.heading: Checking Public IP Address
sections.body: To find your public IP address, you can use various online services or command line tools.

steps.title: Windows
steps.detail: Open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. Look for 'IPv4 Address' under your active network connection.

steps.title: macOS
steps.detail: Open Terminal and type 'ifconfig'. Look for 'inet' under your active network interface (usually 'en0' or 'en1').

steps.title: Linux
steps.detail: Open Terminal and type 'ifconfig' or 'ip addr'. Look for 'inet' under your active network interface.

steps.title: Using Online Tools
steps.detail: Visit websites like 'whatismyip.com' or 'ipinfo.io' to see your public IP address.

faqs.question: What is the difference between local and public IP addresses?
faqs.answer: Local IP addresses are used within a private network, while public IP addresses are assigned by your Internet Service Provider and are used on the internet.

faqs.question: Can I change my public IP address?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can change your public IP address by restarting your router or contacting your ISP, but it may not always be guaranteed.

faqs.question: What should I do if my IP address is not showing up?
faqs.answer: Ensure that your device is connected to the network and try refreshing the command line or online tool. Check your network settings if issues persist.

caveats: The command line tools may vary slightly depending on the operating system version.
